newsitem.title: UK: Hardy Oil says more tests seen for Kelp well.
newsitem.headline: Hardy Oil says more tests seen for Kelp well.

text.p: Hardy Oil & Gas Plc, the independent exploration and production company, said on Monday that further tests are to be carried out to determine the full potential of the Kelp Deep-1 exploration well in the Timor Sea.
The group said operator Mobil Corp has recommended three drill stem tests at different intervals be carried out to further evaluate Kelp's potential.
"Kelp is a high risk, high reward prospect," said chief executive John Walmsley in a statement.
Drilling has reached a depth of 4,670 metres with gas shows.
"Drilling progress to date has been satisfactory. The significance of this well will not be known until the results of the full test programme are available," Walmsley added.
The field, situated in block ZOC-A 95-18 in the Zone of Co-operation jointly administered by Australia and Indonesia, lies 100 km northeast of Hardy Oil's Bayu/Undan gas condensate field.
Hardy holds a 13 percent interest in the block, while Mobil, Royal/Dutch Shell Group and Statoil each hold 25 percent. Mitsubishi Oil Co Ltd holds the other 12 percent.
